question: Why does GRPO training change synthetic metrics but not increase NESTFUL Win Rate?

hypotheses.hypothesis: Reward dispatch bug: all Round-1 arms trained with execution_aware_v3_2_dense; the reward ablation never varied the reward.
evidence_for: train_log.jsonl header + all 160 group rows per arm: reward_policy_resolved=execution_aware_v3_2_dense
console.log: '[v3/run.py] training reward = execution_aware_v3_2_dense' right after '[override] reward.train_policy = reward_ablation_<ARM>'
hash-matched completions across all 10 arm pairs (14-35 matches each) received identical rewards, max_abs_diff=0.0
logged rewards explainable by intended terminal scalars in only 0-5% of rollouts
mechanism reproduced in code: two_phase_train_session setdefault(REWARD_POLICY) + run.py hook env preference

hypotheses.hypothesis: Structural transfer gap between synthetic curriculum and NESTFUL prevents benchmark gains.
evidence_for: gold-tool Jaccard overlap 0.003-0.006 (1-2 shared tools of ~181)
reference-style args in 100% of train rows vs 15-24% of NESTFUL rows; NESTFUL uses str-encoded numbers
train fixed 3-call vs NESTFUL 2-6 calls; offered tools 163 vs 816-3850
pure_stage3_2ep improved train-side signal (loss 0.217->0.063, KL up) while official NESTFUL dropped 1.14pp on n=1661
evidence_against: causality only provable by training on NESTFUL-like data

hypotheses.hypothesis: Round-1 update strength too weak for any behavioral change.
evidence_for: 27-31 optimizer steps at LR 3e-7; KL mean 2.5e-5 to 3.8e-5; clipping ~0; dead groups 21-31%
A0 predicted call sequences identical to C0 on 326/500 (65%); A0 vs A4 identical on 355/500 (71%)
delta_BA Frobenius norm ~0.009 vs lora_A norm 36.66
evidence_against: deltas are nonzero and mutually distinct (delta cosine 0.835-0.885)
stronger update (pure_stage3 2ep) still did not raise NESTFUL

hypotheses.hypothesis: A3 verifiable-process reward causally hurts NESTFUL (53.0%).
evidence_against: A3 trained with the identical reward as every other arm (H1)
53.0-57.4% spread is replicate noise of one config (same seed/data/reward; only rollout nondeterminism differs)

hypotheses.hypothesis: A0/A4 adapters nearly identical (raw LoRA cosine ~1) => no effective training difference.
evidence_against: raw flat cosine dominated by shared seeded lora_A init; artifact
delta-to-init (B@A, float64) cosine A0 vs A4 = 0.835, rel_l2 = 0.575
all 5 FINAL checkpoints have distinct SHA256

hypotheses.hypothesis: Credit assignment bug (good turns punished, executable-wrong rewarded).
evidence_against: 97-99% of good-turn-negative cases are in below-group-mean episodes (expected under outcome-based GRPO)
96-100% of execwrong-positive cases are in all-failure groups (GRPO must rank someone positive)
dead-group flags recompute exactly (parity 100%); no double counting (G0 episode share ~0.19)
hypotheses.untestable_part: matched-prefix / first-divergence audit UNTESTABLE_WITH_CURRENT_LOGS (train rollout trajectories not persisted)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Checkpoint/eval swap, C0 not base, resume/LoRA load-save corruption.
evidence_against: all FINAL SHA256 distinct and equal to adapter_epoch_1
manifests point to correct source runs
C0 win rate reproduced from raw task_results
500/500 paired IDs; win rates and gained/lost reproduce exactly from raw trajectories for every arm
official scorer accepts shorter valid paths (alternative_valid_solution_pass on 254/500 C0 tasks)
hypotheses.known_issue: shared_C0_eval_500 actually ran on 1861 rows (test+dev); its stored 0.5513 win rate is n=1861, not n=500; coverage of the 500 paired IDs is complete so paired analysis is unaffected

hypotheses.hypothesis: v3_2_dense reward is effectively a trace-imitation signal penalizing valid alternative paths.
evidence_for: dense process components are gold-aware; the ablation designed to test this never ran (H1)
evidence_against: official eval scorer accepts alternative paths
counterfactual re-score shows intended policies would have produced substantially different signals (mean reward 0.62-0.76 on identical trajectories)

hypotheses.hypothesis: A4 highest train-side success caused by gated verifiable reward.
evidence_against: metric was a reward-threshold proxy with wrong threshold (0.92; v3_2_dense fully_correct band starts at 0.90)
rewards were identical across arms (H1); difference is rollout noise
2-call weakness pre-exists in C0 (45% vs 62% for 3-call); arms slightly improve it (0.46-0.49)

top_causes_ranked: H1 reward dispatch bug (CONFIRMED, 0.99) - Round-1 ablation invalid as an experiment
H3 Round-1 update too weak for behavioral change (STRONGLY_SUPPORTED, 0.85)
round1_reinterpretation: Round-1 A0-A4 = five replicates of one training config (same seed, data, executor, reward). Win-rate spread 53.0-57.4% on n=500 estimates replicate noise (~±2-4.5pp), not reward-design effects.
